Package hadur2.core.replay

package hadur2.core.replay
Recorded battles as text, and a driver that replays them through a fresh core (CORE-2).

CORE-2 says the core produces identical BotOrders for identical BotInput sequences and identical profile state. This package is how that is checked end to end: hadur2.HadurRecorder in the robot module writes every tick's input and orders from a battle in the real engine, and the replay tests feed the inputs back through Replay.run(java.util.List<java.lang.String>, hadur2.core.port.Telemetry) and compare the orders tick for tick. The melee extension's duel byte-identity also leans on these fixtures: they pin the orchestrator's duel path.

  • LineCodec: one line of text per BotInput (I,...) and per BotOrders (O,...), exact to the bit for every double.
  • Replay: reads a recording (F, N, I and O lines), builds a HadurCore and Guard the way the robot does, and returns the recorded and replayed orders side by side.

Because the tick time reaches the core as a TickTime event measured by the adapter, not from a clock, it is recorded like any other event and a replay makes the same budget decisions (TIME-1, TIME-2) as the live robot did.

Dependencies

This package sits above the core it drives: it depends on hadur2.core (HadurCore, Guard), the model and the ports. ArchUnit (ArchitectureTest.layering) forbids the model, physics and port packages from depending on it. Nothing here does I/O: callers read and write the lines (RES-6), and the core-wide rules (no robocode.*, CORE-1; no randomness, threads, reflection or clock, RES-6; no mutable statics, CORE-2) apply as everywhere in the core.
